## RemediationPolicy

RemediationPolicy says which actions are allowed, on which targets, within which bounds, and whether a human
must approve. Its generation is part of every plan digest, so changing it invalidates pending approvals.
The name must be a DNS label (at most 63 characters), since requests reference it.

- API version: `remediation.shadewright.io/v1alpha1`
- Kind: `RemediationPolicy`
- Scope: Cluster

Validation rules:

- name must be at most 63 characters: `size(self.metadata.name) <= 63`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata` | [ObjectMeta](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#objectmeta-v1-meta) | No | Standard object metadata. |
| `spec` | [RemediationPolicySpec](#remediationpolicyspec) | Yes | spec is the policy. |
| `status` | [RemediationPolicyStatus](#remediationpolicystatus) | No | status is reserved; no controller writes it yet. |

- Scope: Namespaced

## VerificationReport

VerificationReport is the verifier's evidence for one RemediationRequest in Verifying: whether the pods of
the rollout stayed up without a restart or an OOM kill over a window (ADR-0030 section 7). Only the verifier
writes it; the executor reads it as untrusted evidence, bound by spec to the request, and writes the
request's Cleared condition from it. Its name derives from the request UID.

- API version: `remediation.shadewright.io/v1alpha1`
- Kind: `VerificationReport`
- Scope: Namespaced

Validation rules:

- status.sample never decreases: `!has(oldSelf.status) || !has(oldSelf.status.sample) || (has(self.status) && has(self.status.sample) && self.status.sample >= oldSelf.status.sample)`
- status.windowStart only moves forward: `!has(oldSelf.status) || !has(oldSelf.status.windowStart) || (has(self.status) && has(self.status.windowStart) && timestamp(self.status.windowStart) >= timestamp(oldSelf.status.windowStart))`
- status.resets never decreases: `!has(oldSelf.status) || !has(oldSelf.status.resets) || (has(self.status) && has(self.status.resets) && self.status.resets >= oldSelf.status.resets)`
- status.lastReset is kept once set and its time never moves back: `!has(oldSelf.status) || !has(oldSelf.status.lastReset) || (has(self.status) && has(self.status.lastReset) && timestamp(self.status.lastReset.time) >= timestamp(oldSelf.status.lastReset.time))`
- status.troubleResets never decreases: `!has(oldSelf.status) || !has(oldSelf.status.troubleResets) || (has(self.status) && has(self.status.troubleResets) && self.status.troubleResets >= oldSelf.status.troubleResets)`
- status.lastTroubleReset is kept once set and its time never moves back: `!has(oldSelf.status) || !has(oldSelf.status.lastTroubleReset) || (has(self.status) && has(self.status.lastTroubleReset) && timestamp(self.status.lastTroubleReset.time) >= timestamp(oldSelf.status.lastTroubleReset.time))`
- status.oomKill is set once and never changed: `!has(oldSelf.status) || !has(oldSelf.status.oomKill) || (has(self.status) && has(self.status.oomKill) && self.status.oomKill == oldSelf.status.oomKill)`

## Types

Types used by the resources above, in alphabetical order.

### Action

Action is one entry from the action catalog. Exactly the member named by type is set.


Validation rules:

- adjustKedaMaxReplicas must be set if and only if type is AdjustKedaMaxReplicas: `self.type == 'AdjustKedaMaxReplicas' ? has(self.adjustKedaMaxReplicas) : !has(self.adjustKedaMaxReplicas)`
- setContainerMemoryLimit must be set if and only if type is SetContainerMemoryLimit: `self.type == 'SetContainerMemoryLimit' ? has(self.setContainerMemoryLimit) : !has(self.setContainerMemoryLimit)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestSpec](#remediationrequestspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | [ActionType](#actiontype) | Yes | type selects the action.<br>One of `AdjustKedaMaxReplicas`, `SetContainerMemoryLimit` |
| `adjustKedaMaxReplicas` | [AdjustKedaMaxReplicas](#adjustkedamaxreplicas) | No | adjustKedaMaxReplicas holds the parameters for AdjustKedaMaxReplicas.<br>Rule: desiredValue must differ from previousValue |
| `setContainerMemoryLimit` | [SetContainerMemoryLimit](#setcontainermemorylimit) | No | setContainerMemoryLimit holds the parameters for SetContainerMemoryLimit.<br>Rule: desired must differ from previous<br>Rule: previous and desired must be whole bytes<br>Rule: previous must be between 1Mi and 1Ti<br>Rule: desired must be between 1Mi and 1Ti |

### ActionType

ActionType is the closed catalog of remediation actions (ADR-0003). Adding a value needs typed parameters,
policy bounds, a GitOps patcher and a test that it is refused outside its bounds.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `AdjustKedaMaxReplicas`, `SetContainerMemoryLimit`

Used by: [Action](#action), [PolicyAction](#policyaction).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `AdjustKedaMaxReplicas` | ActionAdjustKedaMaxReplicas changes maxReplicaCount of a KEDA ScaledObject. |
| `SetContainerMemoryLimit` | ActionSetContainerMemoryLimit changes the memory limit of one container in a workload's pod template. |

### AdjustKedaMaxReplicas

AdjustKedaMaxReplicas changes spec.maxReplicaCount of a ScaledObject. previousValue must match the file in
Git when the patch is applied, or the plan is stale.


Validation rules:

- desiredValue must differ from previousValue: `self.desiredValue != self.previousValue`

Used by: [Action](#action).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `previousValue` | integer | Yes | previousValue is the value the plan was made against.<br>Maximum: 1000<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `desiredValue` | integer | Yes | desiredValue is the new maxReplicaCount.<br>Maximum: 1000<br>Minimum: 1 |

### AnalysisModels

AnalysisModels names the two model deployments of ADR-0023: a small model for the one structured triage
call, and a stronger one used only on escalation. There is no field for a key: the analyzer authenticates
with its workload identity (Entra ID, design 11.1), so no credential is ever stored in this object. The two
must be different deployments, so the escalation cap cannot be a second budget for the triage model.


Validation rules:

- an escalation model needs a triage model: `!has(self.escalation) || has(self.triage)`
- triage and escalation must not name the same endpoint and deployment: `!has(self.triage) || !has(self.escalation) || (self.triage.endpoint.endsWith('/') ? self.triage.endpoint.substring(0, self.triage.endpoint.size() - 1) : self.triage.endpoint) != (self.escalation.endpoint.endsWith('/') ? self.escalation.endpoint.substring(0, self.escalation.endpoint.size() - 1) : self.escalation.endpoint) || self.triage.deployment.lowerAscii() != self.escalation.deployment.lowerAscii()`

Used by: [AnalysisSettings](#analysissettings).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `triage` | [ModelDeployment](#modeldeployment) | No | triage is the small model for the one structured call on the prepared context, without tools. Left out, no model is called: an incident no runbook matches is handed off to a person, and no unit of spec.analysis.maxAnalysesPerDay is used for it. |
| `escalation` | [ModelDeployment](#modeldeployment) | No | escalation is the stronger model, called with read tools only on the deterministic escalation signals of ADR-0023. Left out, an escalation trigger hands the incident off to a person. |

### AnalysisSettings

AnalysisSettings bounds each model-backed analysis (design 12.3). Every limit has a safe default and a hard
upper bound in the schema. maxAnalysesPerDay is read by the analysis trigger; the other limits and the
models by the analysis loop, which the analyzer starts only with its --triage-model flag.


Used by: [RemediationSettingsSpec](#remediationsettingsspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxAnalysesPerDay` | integer | No | maxAnalysesPerDay limits model-backed analyses per UTC day, across all Incidents; 0 disables the model. 0 to 10000. Defaulted to 100 also when spec.analysis is left out. Read today by the analysis trigger: 0 marks every Incident not due (AnalysisDisabled). The analysis loop reserves one unit per attempt before its first model call (ADR-0025), so the count is enforced while it runs. Replaces the deprecated spec.maxAnalysesPerDay; while that is still set, the lower of the two applies.<br>Default: `100`<br>Maximum: 10000<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `maxContextBytes` | integer | No | maxContextBytes is the most bytes of redacted cluster context (events, pod status, log excerpts, metrics) the context builder puts into one analysis, before the fixed system part of the prompt. 4096 to 262144; the default of 32768 is roughly 8,000 tokens. A context cut at this bound is marked truncated, which is an escalation trigger (ADR-0023).<br>Default: `32768`<br>Maximum: 262144<br>Minimum: 4096 |
| `maxToolSteps` | integer | No | maxToolSteps is the most read tool calls one escalated analysis may make. The triage call has no tools (ADR-0023), so this only bounds escalation. 0 to 16; 0 means escalation gets no tools.<br>Default: `4`<br>Maximum: 16<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `maxOutputTokens` | integer | No | maxOutputTokens is the most output tokens one model call may produce, sent as the request's MaxOutputTokens, so the provider stops there. An analysis makes at most 3 + maxToolSteps model calls: the triage call, one retry after invalid output, and maxToolSteps + 1 escalated turns (an invalid escalated result gets no retry; it is handed off). That bounds its output. 256 to 16384.<br>Default: `2048`<br>Maximum: 16384<br>Minimum: 256 |
| `maxConcurrentAnalyses` | integer | No | maxConcurrentAnalyses is the most analyses that call a model at once. 1 to 8.<br>Default: `1`<br>Maximum: 8<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `models` | [AnalysisModels](#analysismodels) | No | models names the model deployments the analyzer may call. Left out, no model is configured, so no model is called and every incident no runbook matches is handed off to a person.<br>Rule: an escalation model needs a triage model<br>Rule: triage and escalation must not name the same endpoint and deployment |

### CommentCursor

CommentCursor is where the executor's next look at the conversation comments of the request's pull request
starts (ADR-0028 section 3): the durable watermark, so a restart neither reads a comment again as new nor
skips one. It is written in the status update that stores what the look found, just after the last comment
the look judged. Once set it is kept, and since never decreases (CEL on RemediationRequest). Its fields
other than seen mean something only to the code host's adapter.


Validation rules:

- etag is kept only on the first page of a new sweep: `!has(self.etag) || ((!has(self.page) || self.page == 0) && (!has(self.afterID) || self.afterID == 0))`
- evictedAt and evictedID are set together: `has(self.evictedAt) == (has(self.evictedID) && self.evictedID > 0)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `since` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | since is the oldest update time the current sweep of the comments asks for. Every comment created at or before it was returned by an earlier look, so a command in one counts as an edit (EditedAfterSeen). That is an assumption about the code host: the GitHub adapter sets since a minute before the host's time when the previous sweep began, assuming a new comment shows up in the list within a minute. One that shows up later is refused as EditedAfterSeen and has to be posted again: it fails closed. |
| `page` | integer | No | page is the page the next look starts on; 0 starts a new sweep.<br>Maximum: 100000<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `afterID` | integer | No | afterID: the comments of the current sweep with an ID up to this one were returned already.<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `sweepStart` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | sweepStart is the code host's time when the current sweep began. |
| `etag` | string | No | etag is the entity tag of the last answer to the first page of a sweep that held no comment, sent as If-None-Match, so an unchanged answer is "not modified" and costs no read.<br>Maximum length: 256<br>Pattern: `^(W/)?"[!#-~]*"$` |
| `seen` | [SeenComment](#seencomment) array | No | seen are the commands the executor judged whose update time is at or after since, so a look that returns them again unchanged (the overlap of two sweeps) does not judge them again: at most MaxSeenComments, the newest. A comment returned with another update time was edited and is judged again.<br>Maximum items: 50<br>List type: map<br>List key: `commentID` |
| `evictedAt` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | evictedAt is the newest update time of the commands pushed out of seen by its bound; with evictedID it is the watermark of those commands. A command with an ID up to evictedID and an update time up to evictedAt counts as judged, so an evicted one returned again unchanged is not judged again, while one edited after its judgement has a later update time and is. The watermark only grows, and is dropped once since passes evictedAt. A command edited during a sweep and passed by it may count as judged too when more than MaxSeenComments newer ones were judged first: it is then not judged, never accepted twice. Those newer ones include commands from authors without write access, so anyone who can comment can cause this on purpose; it fails closed (the edited command is missed, its author posts a new comment). |
| `evictedID` | integer | No | evictedID is the highest ID of the commands pushed out of seen; set together with evictedAt.<br>Minimum: 0 |

### ConflictSeen

ConflictSeen is when and on which commits the executor first saw its pull request reported with a merge
conflict (PullRequestStatus.conflictSeen).


Used by: [PullRequestStatus](#pullrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | Yes | at is when the executor saw the conflict, on its own clock. |
| `headSHA` | string | Yes | headSHA is the pull request's head at that read, always the recorded head.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `targetHead` | string | Yes | targetHead is the head of the target branch the freshness check read with it. It is a record of what the first report was about; a later move of the target branch does not start the wait again.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |

### GitBranch

GitBranch is a branch name. Names that git or a shell could read as something else (a leading dash,
refs/, HEAD, '..', '.lock') are refused, and so is the shadewright/ prefix Shadewright uses for its own
branches.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 255
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$`

Validation rules:

- must be a plain branch name, not HEAD, refs/..., shadewright/... or one containing '..' or '.lock': `!self.contains('..') && !self.endsWith('.lock') && !self.contains('.lock/') && self != 'HEAD' && !self.startsWith('refs/') && !self.startsWith('shadewright/')`

Used by: [GitRepository](#gitrepository), [MergeReceipt](#mergereceipt), [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource).

### GitDirPath

GitDirPath is a directory relative to a repository root, "." for the root itself. Every segment follows
the rule of GitFilePath, so absolute paths, parent references, hidden directories and option-like names
are refused.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 512
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*)$`

Used by: [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource).

### GitFilePath

GitFilePath is one YAML file, relative to a repository root. Every segment starts with a letter, digit or
underscore, so absolute paths, parent references, hidden directories such as .github, option-like names
and wildcards are all refused.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 512
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*\.ya?ml$`

Used by: [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource).

### GitHubRepository

GitHubRepository holds the GitHub App settings for one repository.


Used by: [GitRepository](#gitrepository).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appClientID` | string | Yes | appClientID is the GitHub App's client ID: 1 to 64 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'.<br>Maximum length: 64<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` |
| `installationID` | integer | Yes | installationID is the App's installation that covers this repository.<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `signer` | [Signer](#signer) | Yes | signer says where the App's private key is.<br>Rule: a signer must be configured |

### GitPathPattern

GitPathPattern is a glob, relative to a repository root, for files a policy may patch. `*` matches within one
path segment and `**` across segments; neither matches a segment that starts with a dot. The first segment
must be literal, so a pattern cannot cover the whole repository, and no segment may start with a dot or a
dash.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 512
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_*][A-Za-z0-9_.*-]*)*$`

Validation rules:

- must not contain '..': `!self.contains('..')`

Used by: [PolicyGitOps](#policygitops).

### GitProviderType

GitProviderType names a Git hosting adapter (ADR-0004, ADR-0013).

- Underlying type: string
- One of `GitHub`

Used by: [GitRepository](#gitrepository).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `GitHub` | GitProviderGitHub uses a GitHub App. |

### GitRepository

GitRepository is a repository Shadewright may open pull requests in. Requests and policies refer to it by
name, so the model never chooses a URL or credentials.


Validation rules:

- github must be set if and only if provider is GitHub: `self.provider == 'GitHub' ? has(self.github) : !has(self.github)`
- a GitHub repository URL must be https://github.com/&lt;owner>/&lt;repo> in lower case, without .git: `self.provider != 'GitHub' || (self.url.matches('^https://github[.]com/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}/[a-z0-9_.-]{1,100}$') && !self.url.endsWith('.git') && !self.url.endsWith('/.') && !self.url.endsWith('/..'))`
- a GitHub target branch must start with a letter or digit, have at most 200 characters and not end with '.': `self.provider != 'GitHub' || (self.targetBranch.matches('^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,199}$') && !self.targetBranch.endsWith('.'))`

Used by: [RemediationSettingsSpec](#remediationsettingsspec).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [Name](#name) | Yes | name is how policies and requests refer to the repository.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `url` | string | Yes | url is the HTTPS clone URL, without credentials, query or fragment, and without a path segment that is '.' or '..'. It must match the URL of the Flux source that delivers a target, or no change is made. For GitHub it is https://github.com/&lt;owner>/&lt;repo> in lower case, without .git: an owner of 1 to 39 letters, digits and hyphens that starts with a letter or digit, and a repository name of 1 to 100 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' other than '.' and '..' (it may start with '.', as in .github).<br>Maximum length: 512<br>Pattern: <code>^https://&#91;a-z0-9.-]+(:&#91;0-9]+)?(/(\.?&#91;A-Za-z0-9_~-]&#91;A-Za-z0-9_.~-]*&#124;\.\.&#91;A-Za-z0-9_.~-]+))+$</code> |
| `targetBranch` | [GitBranch](#gitbranch) | No | targetBranch is the only branch pull requests may target. The branch Flux tracks must equal it. For GitHub it starts with a letter or digit, has at most 200 characters and does not end with '.'.<br>Default: `main`<br>Maximum length: 255<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$`<br>Rule: must be a plain branch name, not HEAD, refs/..., shadewright/... or one containing '..' or '.lock' |
| `provider` | [GitProviderType](#gitprovidertype) | Yes | provider selects the Git hosting adapter.<br>One of `GitHub` |
| `github` | [GitHubRepository](#githubrepository) | No | github holds GitHub App settings. |

### Handoff

Handoff records the supersede handoff (ADR-0028 section 4), written in this order: the replacement's
admission sets from (phase Reserved); one write on the predecessor sets to (phase Intent) and its hint
Reserved; after the branch update the replacement's from moves to Done, then the predecessor ends Superseded
with HandedOff, its to Done and its hint Consumed. A request in the middle of a chain has both: from for the
handoff that gave it the pull request, to for the one that passes it on. Each side starts in its first phase
and is never removed: from changes only its phase and, once Done, the record of the rewrite
(pullRequestUpdate); to changes only its phase, except that an Aborted one is replaced by the Intent of a
later replacement.


Validation rules:

- a handoff has from, to or both: `has(self.from) || has(self.to)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [IncomingHandoff](#incominghandoff) | No | from is the incoming side, set on a replacement.<br>Rule: an incoming handoff is Reserved, Done or Aborted<br>Rule: an incoming handoff is pinned: only its phase changes<br>Rule: the rewrite after a handoff is recorded only once it is Done<br>Rule: the record of the pull request's rewrite never changes once set<br>Rule: an incoming handoff moves only from Reserved to Done or Aborted |
| `to` | [OutgoingHandoff](#outgoinghandoff) | No | to is the outgoing side, set on a predecessor.<br>Rule: an outgoing handoff is Intent, Done or Aborted<br>Rule: an outgoing handoff is pinned: only its phase changes, or an Aborted one is replaced<br>Rule: an outgoing handoff moves only from Intent to Done or Aborted, or from Aborted to the Intent of another replacement for another hint |

### HandoffPhase

HandoffPhase is how far one side of a handoff has come. Incoming, on the replacement: Reserved (it took the
target lock and named its predecessor), then Done (it holds the pull request) or Aborted. Outgoing, on the
predecessor: Intent (it expects its replacement's commit on top of expectedHead), then Done (it ended
Superseded with HandedOff) or Aborted. Each side starts in its first phase and moves only once; an outgoing
side that was Aborted may be replaced by the Intent of a later replacement for another hint.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `Reserved`, `Intent`, `Done`, `Aborted`

Used by: [IncomingHandoff](#incominghandoff), [OutgoingHandoff](#outgoinghandoff).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Reserved` |  |
| `Intent` |  |
| `Done` |  |
| `Aborted` |  |

### HandoffStep

HandoffStep is the record of a step after a handoff that the Git host either did or refused for good.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `Done`, `Refused`

Used by: [IncomingHandoff](#incominghandoff).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Done` | HandoffStepDone: the Git host did the step. |
| `Refused` | HandoffStepRefused: the Git host refused the step for good (a permission the App lacks, a rule, an invalid request); it is not asked again. |

### Hint

Hint is one reviewer hint the executor accepted from a comment on the request's pull request (ADR-0028
section 2): its author had write access when it was accepted, its text is redacted and bounded, and it is
pinned by comment ID, digest and the comment's updatedAt. Only the executor writes it; the analyzer reads
the stored text, never the comment.


Validation rules:

- text must be at most 2048 bytes: `size(bytes(self.text)) <= 2048`
- a Declined hint needs a reason: `self.state != 'Declined' || has(self.reason)`
- a stored hint is pinned: only its state and reason change: `self.source == oldSelf.source && self.commentID == oldSelf.commentID && self.digest == oldSelf.digest && self.text == oldSelf.text && self.author == oldSelf.author && self.updatedAt == oldSelf.updatedAt && self.acceptedAt == oldSelf.acceptedAt`
- the reason of a Consumed or Declined hint never changes: `!(oldSelf.state in ['Consumed', 'Declined']) || (has(self.reason) == has(oldSelf.reason) && (!has(self.reason) || self.reason == oldSelf.reason))`
- editedAfterAccept is never unset: `!has(oldSelf.editedAfterAccept) || !oldSelf.editedAfterAccept || (has(self.editedAfterAccept) && self.editedAfterAccept)`
- the outcome of a hint never changes once set: `!has(oldSelf.outcome) || (has(self.outcome) && self.outcome == oldSelf.outcome)`
- a hint moves only from Pending to Reserved or Declined, and from Reserved to Consumed or Declined: `oldSelf.state == self.state || (oldSelf.state == 'Pending' && self.state in ['Reserved', 'Declined']) || (oldSelf.state == 'Reserved' && self.state in ['Consumed', 'Declined'])`
- only a Consumed or Declined hint has a reply: `!has(self.reply) || self.state in ['Consumed', 'Declined']`
- the reply of a hint never changes once set: `!has(oldSelf.reply) || (has(self.reply) && self.reply == oldSelf.reply)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [HintSource](#hintsource) | Yes | source is the system the comment is in.<br>One of `GitHub` |
| `commentID` | integer | Yes | commentID is the comment's ID in the source.<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `author` | [HintAuthor](#hintauthor) | Yes | author wrote the comment. |
| `text` | string | Yes | text is the hint after redaction, at most 2048 bytes. It is untrusted input: the analysis fences it as a reviewer's opinion, never as instructions or evidence.<br>Maximum length: 2048<br>Minimum length: 1 |
| `digest` | string | Yes | digest is the SHA-256 of text.<br>Pattern: `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `updatedAt` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | Yes | updatedAt is the comment's updated time when the hint was accepted. A comment whose updated time differs later was edited after acceptance, and the edit is ignored. |
| `acceptedAt` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | Yes | acceptedAt is when the executor accepted the hint. |
| `state` | [HintState](#hintstate) | Yes | state says what became of the hint.<br>One of `Pending`, `Reserved`, `Consumed`, `Declined` |
| `reason` | string | No | reason says why a Declined hint was declined: the analysis's outcome (for example BudgetSpent or NoProposal), NoAnswer when none came within the executor's bound, or the end of the request (PullRequestMerged, PullRequestClosed, RequestEnded), or the end of its replacement without the handoff: ReplacementDenied when the replacement was Denied, HandoffAborted when it ended otherwise, or HintsTurnedOff when the executor runs with reviewer hints off, which declines every Pending or Reserved hint. HintDeclineReasons lists them.<br>One of `NoModelConfigured`, `BudgetSpent`, `BudgetUnavailable`, `NoProposal`, `MissingData`, `NoEvidence`, `TargetNotSupported`, `PreviousValueUnknown`, `NoChange`, `DirectionReversed`, `NoPolicyForAction`, `ActionOutOfBounds`, `InvalidOutput`, `EscalationNotConfigured`, `StepLimit`, `TokenLimit`, `DeadlineExceeded`, `ModelUnavailable`, `ModelNotFound`, `ModelForbidden`, `ModelError`, `UnexpectedModel`, `EndpointNotAllowed`, `PlanUnchanged`, `HintNotPending`, `RequestNotCreated`, `CoolingDown`, `NoAnswer`, `PullRequestMerged`, `PullRequestClosed`, `RequestEnded`, `ReplacementDenied`, `HandoffAborted`, `HintsTurnedOff` |
| `editedAfterAccept` | boolean | No | editedAfterAccept is true once the executor saw the comment edited after it accepted the hint. The stored text stays as it was; the edit is recorded once, here, whatever the number of edits. |
| `outcome` | string | No | outcome is the analysis's outcome that answered the hint with a replacement (Proposed or RunbookMatched), recorded when the executor first read it in the Incident. The hint is answered from then on, whatever the Incident handles later: it waits for the handoff, and the answer timeout no longer applies. Once set it never changes.<br>One of `Proposed`, `RunbookMatched` |
| `reply` | [HintReply](#hintreply) | No | reply records the executor's reply to this hint in the pull request, once the hint is Declined or Consumed (ADR-0028 section 7). Once set it never changes.<br>One of `Posted`, `NotRedactable`, `TooManyComments`, `Refused`, `GaveUp` |

### HintRefusal

HintRefusal says why the executor stored no hint for a writer's comment that carried the command (ADR-0028
section 2); a command of an author without write access is never recorded, so it cannot push a record out.
CapReached: MaxHints hints of the request are Consumed or Reserved already, which count for its whole
supersede chain. TooLong: the hint is over MaxHintTextBytes after redaction, or the body was cut before the
end of its first line. NotRedactable: the redacted text still holds something the redactor would change.
Empty: the command has no text. EditedAfterSeen: a comment the executor had read already was edited to carry
the command. An edit of a stored hint's comment is recorded on the hint (editedAfterAccept), not here.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `CapReached`, `TooLong`, `NotRedactable`, `Empty`, `EditedAfterSeen`

Used by: [RefusedHint](#refusedhint).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `CapReached` |  |
| `TooLong` |  |
| `NotRedactable` |  |
| `Empty` |  |
| `EditedAfterSeen` |  |

### HintReply

HintReply records what became of the executor's reply to a hint, or to a refused command, in the pull
request (ADR-0028 section 7). The reply is built from a fixed template and typed fields, plus the quoted
first line of the stored hint, its one free text. It is posted only when the redactor would change nothing
in it, so it fails closed. Posted: the reply is in the pull request (posted, or found there by its marker
in a comment of the executor's own). NotRedactable: the redactor would still change the reply, so nothing
was posted. TooManyComments: the pull request has more comments than the executor reads to find an
earlier reply, so nothing was posted rather than risk a second reply. Refused: the Git host refused the
comment for good (a permission the App lacks, a rule, an invalid request). GaveUp: posting failed on every
try within the executor's bound. Only Posted means the author was told.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `Posted`, `NotRedactable`, `TooManyComments`, `Refused`, `GaveUp`

Used by: [Hint](#hint), [RefusedHint](#refusedhint).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Posted` |  |
| `NotRedactable` |  |
| `TooManyComments` |  |
| `Refused` |  |
| `GaveUp` |  |

### IncidentSpec

IncidentSpec identifies a group of similar symptoms (design section 3.2). It is immutable: a different
fingerprint is a different incident.


Validation rules:

- spec is immutable; a different symptom is a new Incident: `self == oldSelf`
- occurrenceNumber and previousIncident are set together: `has(self.occurrenceNumber) == has(self.previousIncident)`
- previousIncident must be the occurrence before this one of the same fingerprint: `!has(self.occurrenceNumber) || (self.occurrenceNumber == 2 ? self.previousIncident == 'incident-' + self.fingerprint.substring(7) : (self.previousIncident.startsWith('incident-' + self.fingerprint.substring(7) + '-') && self.previousIncident.size() > 74 && int(self.previousIncident.substring(74)) == self.occurrenceNumber - 1))`

Used by: [Incident](#incident).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fingerprint` | string | Yes | fingerprint is the hash of cluster, namespace, owner, reason, action, type, reporting controller and normalized symptom.<br>Maximum length: 71<br>Pattern: `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `subject` | [ObjectRef](#objectref) | Yes | subject is the object the symptoms are correlated to: the owning workload when there is one. |
| `reason` | string | Yes | reason is the event reason or status reason, for example FailedScheduling or OOMKilled.<br>Maximum length: 128<br>Minimum length: 1 |
| `type` | string | No | type is the event type.<br>Default: `Warning`<br>One of `Normal`, `Warning` |
| `reportingController` | string | No | reportingController is the component that reported the symptom.<br>Maximum length: 253 |
| `symptom` | string | No | symptom is the normalized, redacted description: variable parts removed, secrets never included.<br>Maximum length: 1024 |
| `occurrenceNumber` | integer | No | occurrenceNumber is which Incident of the fingerprint this is: absent for the first, n >= 2 for the Incident the analyzer opened when the symptom was seen again more than 24 hours after the previous one was resolved (design 3.2). The name carries it as the suffix "-&lt;n>".<br>Maximum: 999999<br>Minimum: 2 |
| `previousIncident` | string | No | previousIncident is the name of the Incident of the same fingerprint before this one, occurrence n-1, set together with occurrenceNumber. It is a link for people only: the analysis never reads it, so no earlier outcome or policy decision reaches the model (invariant 1).<br>Maximum length: 80<br>Pattern: <code>^incident-&#91;0-9a-f]{64}(-(&#91;2-9]&#124;&#91;1-9]&#91;0-9]{1,5}))?$</code> |

### IncidentStatus

IncidentStatus holds the deduplication state that must survive restarts (ADR-0007). No logs or transcripts.


Validation rules:

- resolvedTime cannot change while the phase stays Resolved: `!(has(oldSelf.phase) && oldSelf.phase == 'Resolved' && has(oldSelf.resolvedTime) && has(self.phase) && self.phase == 'Resolved') || (has(self.resolvedTime) && self.resolvedTime == oldSelf.resolvedTime)`
- revertsProposed only grows: an entry is never removed, and its state only moves from Pending to Created: `!has(oldSelf.revertsProposed) || (has(self.revertsProposed) && oldSelf.revertsProposed.all(o, self.revertsProposed.exists(n, n.uid == o.uid && n.name == o.name && (o.state == 'Pending' || n.state == 'Created'))))`

Used by: [Incident](#incident).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `phase` | [IncidentPhase](#incidentphase) | No | phase summarizes the incident.<br>One of `Open`, `Analyzing`, `Proposed`, `Escalated`, `Resolved` |
| `firstSeen` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | firstSeen is when the first observation arrived. |
| `lastSeen` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | lastSeen is when the latest observation arrived. |
| `count` | integer | No | count is the number of occurrences counted, counting event series increments, not totals. It saturates at 1,000,000: a series count is written by whoever can create events, so forged updates can raise it without bound otherwise. It is not a count of distinct occurrences.<br>Maximum: 1000000<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `occurrences` | [OccurrenceRecord](#occurrencerecord) array | No | occurrences are the newest occurrences counted for this incident, newest first, at most 32: for each, the highest total the cluster reported that was counted, and when it began. After a restart the analyzer reads them to count only what is new. Older ones are dropped.<br>Maximum items: 32<br>List type: atomic |
| `occurrencesDroppedThrough` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | occurrencesDroppedThrough is when the newest occurrence dropped from occurrences began. An occurrence with no record that began no later than this is treated as counted in full, so the bound never counts one twice. |
| `resolvedTime` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | resolvedTime is when the Incident moved to phase Resolved, written in the same status update (design 3.2). It cannot change while the phase stays Resolved. A symptom seen again within 24 hours of it, or with it missing, moves the Incident to Escalated without an analysis; seen again later, it opens the next occurrence of the fingerprint as a new Incident. |
| `lastAnalysisTime` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | lastAnalysisTime is when the analyzer last ran; it drives the cooldown. |
| `handledHint` | [HintRef](#hintref) | No | handledHint is the reviewer hint the analysis claimed by lastAnalysisTime answers (ADR-0028 section 3): written in the status update that takes the claim and kept with the outcome in the Analyzed condition, so a restarted analyzer does not run the same hint twice and the executor can match a refusal to the hint. Absent for an analysis without a hint. The trigger also writes it, with the Analyzed reason CoolingDown or BudgetSpent, for a hint it refuses without an analysis. |
| `analysisRecords` | [RecordID](#recordid) array | No | analysisRecords are the newest analysis record IDs, oldest first (at most MaxAnalysisRecords).<br>Maximum items: 20<br>Maximum length: 200<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,199}$`<br>List type: atomic |
| `remediationRequests` | [Name](#name) array | No | remediationRequests are the names of requests made for this incident, oldest first.<br>Maximum items: 20<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`<br>List type: atomic |
| `revertsProposed` | [ProposedRevert](#proposedrevert) array | No | revertsProposed are the failed requests of this incident, by name and UID, that the analyzer's revert proposer decided to revert (ADR-0030 section 8, #96), oldest first. The proposer writes an entry in state Pending before it creates the revert and moves it to Created once the revert exists; it never takes a new decision for a request listed here, so a failed request gets one revert for good, also after that revert was deleted. Entries are never removed and a state never moves back; a full list stops new reverts for this incident instead (condition RevertsStopped).<br>Maximum items: 20<br>List type: map<br>List key: `uid` |
| `conditions` | [Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#condition-v1-meta) array | No | conditions explain the phase.<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type` |

### IncomingHandoff

IncomingHandoff is the replacement's side of a handoff: the predecessor it takes over and the hint it
answers, equal to spec.replaces. Once written, only its phase and the record of the rewrite after it change.
The check run shadewright/review is not recorded here: it belongs to each head of the pull request, also
one no handoff pushed (PullRequestStatus.reviewCheck).


Validation rules:

- an incoming handoff is Reserved, Done or Aborted: `self.phase in ['Reserved', 'Done', 'Aborted']`
- an incoming handoff is pinned: only its phase changes: `self.name == oldSelf.name && self.uid == oldSelf.uid && self.hint == oldSelf.hint`
- the rewrite after a handoff is recorded only once it is Done: `!has(self.pullRequestUpdate) || self.phase == 'Done'`
- the record of the pull request's rewrite never changes once set: `!has(oldSelf.pullRequestUpdate) || (has(self.pullRequestUpdate) && self.pullRequestUpdate == oldSelf.pullRequestUpdate)`
- an incoming handoff moves only from Reserved to Done or Aborted: `oldSelf.phase == self.phase || (oldSelf.phase == 'Reserved' && self.phase in ['Done', 'Aborted'])`

Used by: [Handoff](#handoff).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [Name](#name) | Yes | name of the predecessor.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `uid` | [UID](#uid) | Yes | uid of the predecessor.<br>Maximum length: 36<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| `hint` | [HintRef](#hintref) | Yes | hint is the predecessor's hint the replacement answers. |
| `phase` | [HandoffPhase](#handoffphase) | Yes | phase is how far this side has come.<br>One of `Reserved`, `Intent`, `Done`, `Aborted` |
| `pullRequestUpdate` | [HandoffStep](#handoffstep) | No | pullRequestUpdate records the rewrite of the pull request's title and body for this request's plan, with its marker (ADR-0028 section 4, step 6): Done once the Git host did it, Refused when it refused it for good. Until it is Done the body carries the predecessor's marker, or after refused rewrites further up the chain an earlier request's, which this request accepts as its own while its chain reaches that request.<br>One of `Done`, `Refused` |

### IntegrationStatus

IntegrationStatus reports one integration module that is enabled, detected or both. It is a report only:
the analyzer never reads it back to decide which integrations are active, it decides again from
spec.modules and live detection each time.


Validation rules:

- version is set if and only if the integration is detected: `self.detected == has(self.version)`
- an integration that is not detected is not active: `!self.active || self.detected`

Used by: [RemediationSettingsStatus](#remediationsettingsstatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [ModuleName](#modulename) | Yes | name is the integration module.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `detected` | boolean | Yes | detected is true when the cluster serves one of the group versions the module declares. An enabled name that no compiled-in module has is never detected. |
| `version` | string | No | version is the group version that detected the add-on, in discovery form (keda.sh/v1alpha1). Set if and only if the add-on is detected.<br>Maximum length: 253<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: <code>^(&#91;a-z0-9](&#91;-a-z0-9]*&#91;a-z0-9])?(\.&#91;a-z0-9](&#91;-a-z0-9]*&#91;a-z0-9])?)*/)?v&#91;0-9]+((alpha&#124;beta)&#91;0-9]+)?$</code> |
| `active` | boolean | Yes | active is true when the module contributes hooks: it is enabled in spec.modules.integrations and detected. It reports that decision and never feeds it. |

### MemoryLimitBounds

MemoryLimitBounds bounds SetContainerMemoryLimit. Decreases are refused unless maxDecreasePercent is set.


Validation rules:

- min and max must be whole bytes: `quantity(string(self.min)).isInteger() && quantity(string(self.max)).isInteger()`
- min must be at least 1Mi: `quantity(string(self.min)).compareTo(quantity('1Mi')) >= 0`
- max must be at most 1Ti: `quantity(string(self.max)).compareTo(quantity('1Ti')) <= 0`
- min must not be greater than max: `quantity(string(self.min)).compareTo(quantity(string(self.max))) <= 0`

MergeReceipt binds a merge to the repository, branch, pull request and head it was made from (ADR-0030
section 1). The executor writes it in the status write that sets Merged, only for a merge that holds exactly
the planned change and has a full merge commit ID, and never changes it after; every later check of the
merge (delivery, ancestry) reads it instead of the live settings.


Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| `targetBranch` | [GitBranch](#gitbranch) | Yes | targetBranch is the branch the pull request merged into, copied from status.source.targetBranch.<br>Maximum length: 255<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$`<br>Rule: must be a plain branch name, not HEAD, refs/..., shadewright/... or one containing '..' or '.lock' |
| `pullRequest` | integer | Yes | pullRequest is the number of the merged pull request.<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `headSHA` | string | Yes | headSHA is the head that was merged: the commit Shadewright pushed, or the replacement's commit after a handoff. It equals status.pullRequest.headSHA when the receipt is written.<br>Maximum length: 40<br>Minimum length: 40<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `mergeCommitSHA` | string | Yes | mergeCommitSHA is the commit the Git host reports for the merge. It equals status.pullRequest.mergeCommitSHA (a validation rule on the object).<br>Maximum length: 40<br>Minimum length: 40<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `mergedAt` | [MicroTime](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#microtime-v1-meta) | Yes | mergedAt is when the executor recorded the merge: status.pullRequest.mergedAt of the same status write. |

### ModelDeployment

ModelDeployment is one model deployment behind an inference endpoint, for example in Microsoft Foundry
(ADR-0016). It holds no key, token or other credential.


Used by: [AnalysisModels](#analysismodels).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `endpoint` | string | Yes | endpoint is the HTTPS base URL of the inference endpoint, for example https://&lt;resource>.services.ai.azure.com/ or https://&lt;resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1. At most 256 characters: a host name of lower-case DNS labels whose last label starts with a letter (so no IP address and no single-label host such as localhost), an optional port from 1 to 65535 and an optional path whose segments do not start with '.'. No user info, query or fragment. The schema is vendor-neutral (ADR-0013). The endpoint decides where the analyzer's Entra ID token and the redacted context go: the analyzer refuses a host outside the allow-list of suffixes of its --model-endpoint-suffixes flag (not in this object) or a port other than 443, refuses private, loopback and link-local addresses when it dials, and requests a token for the Cognitive Services audience only.<br>Maximum length: 256<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: <code>^https://(&#91;a-z0-9](&#91;a-z0-9-]{0,61}&#91;a-z0-9])?\.)+&#91;a-z](&#91;a-z0-9-]{0,61}&#91;a-z0-9])?(:(&#91;1-9]&#91;0-9]{0,3}&#124;&#91;1-5]&#91;0-9]{4}&#124;6&#91;0-4]&#91;0-9]{3}&#124;65&#91;0-4]&#91;0-9]{2}&#124;655&#91;0-2]&#91;0-9]&#124;6553&#91;0-5]))?(/&#91;A-Za-z0-9_~-]&#91;A-Za-z0-9._~-]*)*/?$</code> |
| `deployment` | string | Yes | deployment is the name of the model deployment: 1 to 64 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit.<br>Maximum length: 64<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` |
| `apiVersion` | string | Yes | apiVersion is the inference API version the adapter sends: v1, or a date such as 2024-10-21 (month 01 to 12, day 01 to 31), optionally followed by -preview.<br>Maximum length: 32<br>Minimum length: 2<br>Pattern: <code>^(v1&#124;&#91;0-9]{4}-(0&#91;1-9]&#124;1&#91;0-2])-(0&#91;1-9]&#124;&#91;12]&#91;0-9]&#124;3&#91;01])(-preview)?)$</code> |
| `maxTokensPerDay` | integer | Yes | maxTokensPerDay is the daily spend cap of this deployment, in tokens per UTC day: input (cached or not) plus output tokens of every call, a failed or timed-out call counted at its upper bound (the input estimate plus maxOutputTokens). Required, with no default, so the admin chooses the cap of each deployment. It is a count of tokens, not an amount of money, because tokens are what the provider reports and bills, they are whole numbers, and a money cap would need a price list in this object that goes stale. It is per deployment because the triage and escalation models differ in price. The spend it allows is at most this count times the deployment's highest price per token (design 12.1) only because the counter reserves a call's upper bound before calling, under one lock for concurrent analyses (planned, #208). 0 to 1,000,000,000; 0, or a cap that is spent, stops calls to this deployment and hands the incident off.<br>Maximum: 1000000000<br>Minimum: 0 |

### ModuleName

ModuleName names a cluster platform or integration module (design 2.4 and 2.5): a DNS label that starts with
a letter, at most 63 characters, the rule internal/modules checks when it builds its registry (a test keeps
the two equal). It is a pattern, not a list of known names, so a module compiled into a later release, or
shipped as a pack (ADR-0019), needs no schema change. A name that no compiled-in module has is accepted and
contributes nothing.

- Underlying type: string
- Maximum length: 63
- Minimum length: 1
- Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `generic` |  |

### Modules

Modules says which platform and integration modules the cluster admin enables (ADR-0018). Platform and
integration names are separate namespaces, so they are enabled in separate lists. A module contributes hooks
(symptom sources, diagnosis rules, tools, actions) only when it is enabled here and the analyzer detects it:
detection only reports and narrows, it never enables a module, and a module that is enabled but not
detected contributes nothing. Which modules are active is always worked out again from these lists and live
detection, never read back from status, which is only a report.


Used by: [RemediationSettingsSpec](#remediationsettingsspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platforms` | [ModuleName](#modulename) array | No | platforms are the platform modules enabled besides generic, which is always on and is not listed. More than one may be listed, so one settings file can serve clusters on different platforms: only the one the analyzer detects is active. Empty means generic only. The cap of 8 is also the most platform modules besides generic one binary may compile in (internal/modules refuses more), so every one of them can be enabled.<br>Maximum items: 8<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`<br>List type: set<br>Rule: the generic platform is always on and is not listed (`!('generic' in self)`) |
| `integrations` | [ModuleName](#modulename) array | No | integrations are the integration modules enabled. Each is active only while the analyzer detects its add-on. Empty means none. The cap of 32 is also the most integration modules one binary may compile in (internal/modules refuses more), so every one of them can be enabled.<br>Maximum items: 32<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`<br>List type: set |

### OutgoingHandoff

OutgoingHandoff is the predecessor's side of a handoff: the replacement that takes it over, the hint of this
request it answers (which must be in status.hints, in the state its phase implies: Reserved while Intent,
Consumed once Done, Declined once Aborted) and the branch head the replacement's commit must have as its
parent. Only its phase changes once written, except that an Aborted one is replaced by the Intent of a later
replacement, for another hint of this request.


Validation rules:

- an outgoing handoff is Intent, Done or Aborted: `self.phase in ['Intent', 'Done', 'Aborted']`
- an outgoing handoff is pinned: only its phase changes, or an Aborted one is replaced: `(oldSelf.phase == 'Aborted' && self.phase == 'Intent') || (self.name == oldSelf.name && self.uid == oldSelf.uid && self.hint == oldSelf.hint && self.expectedHead == oldSelf.expectedHead)`
- an outgoing handoff moves only from Intent to Done or Aborted, or from Aborted to the Intent of another replacement for another hint: `oldSelf.phase == self.phase || (oldSelf.phase == 'Intent' && self.phase in ['Done', 'Aborted']) || (oldSelf.phase == 'Aborted' && self.phase == 'Intent' && self.uid != oldSelf.uid && (self.hint.source != oldSelf.hint.source || self.hint.commentID != oldSelf.hint.commentID))`

Used by: [Handoff](#handoff).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [Name](#name) | Yes | name of the replacement.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `uid` | [UID](#uid) | Yes | uid of the replacement, so a request recreated under the same name is never taken for it.<br>Maximum length: 36<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| `hint` | [HintRef](#hintref) | Yes | hint is this request's hint the replacement answers. |
| `expectedHead` | string | Yes | expectedHead is the head of the branch when the intent was recorded: the replacement's commit must have it as its parent.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `phase` | [HandoffPhase](#handoffphase) | Yes | phase is how far this side has come.<br>One of `Reserved`, `Intent`, `Done`, `Aborted` |

### PlatformStatus

PlatformStatus reports which platform the analyzer detected and which one it uses. They differ when the
detected platform is not enabled in spec.modules.platforms: the analyzer then falls back to generic. So the
three cases are: nothing detected (detected left out, active generic), detected and enabled (active equal to
detected), and detected but not enabled (active generic). It is a report only: the analyzer never reads it
back to decide which platform to use, it decides again from spec.modules and live detection each time.


Validation rules:

- detected is left out, not generic, when no platform claims the cluster: `!has(self.detected) || self.detected != 'generic'`
- active is generic or the detected platform: `self.active == 'generic' || (has(self.detected) && self.active == self.detected)`

Used by: [RemediationSettingsStatus](#remediationsettingsstatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

### PullRequestStatus

PullRequestStatus records the pull request that carries the plan.


Validation rules:

- appliedObservedAt needs mergeCommitSHA: `!has(self.appliedObservedAt) || has(self.mergeCommitSHA)`
- reviewCheck names the recorded head: `!has(self.reviewCheck) || self.reviewCheck.head == self.headSHA`
- conflictSeen names the recorded head: `!has(self.conflictSeen) || self.conflictSeen.headSHA == self.headSHA`

Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | integer | Yes | number of the pull request.<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `url` | string | Yes | url of the pull request.<br>Maximum length: 2048<br>Pattern: `^https://` |
| `headSHA` | string | Yes | headSHA is the commit Shadewright pushed. Any other head stops automation.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `renderedTargetHead` | string | No | renderedTargetHead is the head of the target branch at which the change in the pull request was last rendered and found to be exactly the planned one. While the pull request waits, the change is rendered again only when the target branch head is another commit; empty means not rendered since it was recorded.<br>Maximum length: 40<br>Minimum length: 40<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `mergeCommitSHA` | string | No | mergeCommitSHA is the commit the Git host reports the pull request was merged as, recorded when Shadewright sees the merge of the pull request it pushed. Delivery is checked against it: the GitOps controller must report this commit, or a later commit of the target branch containing it, as applied. Empty until then, and when the host reported none. Once set it never changes.<br>Maximum length: 40<br>Minimum length: 40<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `appliedObservedAt` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | appliedObservedAt is when the executor first saw the GitOps controller report mergeCommitSHA, or a later commit of the target branch that holds it, as applied and Ready. It is set once and never moved, so a deadline measured from it (the rollout check, condition RolledOut) cannot be pushed back. Written only for a Deployment or StatefulSet target delivered by a Flux Kustomization, within an hour of the merge. |
| `mergedAt` | [MicroTime](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#microtime-v1-meta) | No | mergedAt is when the executor first recorded the request Merged, set in the status write that sets the phase and never moved, unlike lastPhaseTransitionTime, which every later phase moves. A duplicate of the same Incident and target created before it ends Superseded (reason AnotherRequestMerged, #556). Empty on a request merged before the field existed. |
| `reviewCheck` | [ReviewCheck](#reviewcheck) | No | reviewCheck is the state of the check run shadewright/review on headSHA (ADR-0028 section 5, the merge gate), written only with reviewer hints on: InProgress once the executor created it on that head, Passed once it completed it with success after an approval of that head by someone who wrote no hint in the chain, Failed when the executor could not read every review of the pull request and completed it with failure (it fails closed; condition Approved False with reason ReviewListTooLong), Refused when the Git host refused to create or complete it for good (condition Approved then says so). It always names headSHA: a new head starts without it, so a state never outlives its head.<br>Rule: on one head the check run moves only from InProgress to Passed, Failed or Refused |
| `conflictSeen` | [ConflictSeen](#conflictseen) | No | conflictSeen records the first read in which the Git host reported this pull request open with a merge conflict while the plan was fresh. GitHub computes mergeability lazily and may report a stale conflict, so one read does not end the request: it ends NeedsIntervention with reason ChangeRequestConflict only on a later conflicted read, with the plan still fresh, at least two minutes after at, on the same head and target branch head. Any read that finds no conflict (an unknown answer included) removes it, and a new target branch head starts the wait again. Only the executor writes it. |

| `reason` | [HintRefusal](#hintrefusal) | Yes | reason says why no hint was stored.<br>One of `CapReached`, `TooLong`, `NotRedactable`, `Empty`, `EditedAfterSeen` |

### RemediationMode

RemediationMode says how a plan is carried out. GitOps is the only mode (ADR-0003).

- Underlying type: string
- One of `GitOps`

Used by: [RemediationRequestSpec](#remediationrequestspec).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `GitOps` | RemediationModeGitOps changes the cluster only through a pull request to the GitOps repository. |

### RemediationPhase

RemediationPhase summarizes where a request is. Conditions carry the reasons.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `Pending`, `PolicyChecked`, `PRCreated`, `AwaitingApproval`, `AutoMergeQueued`, `Merged`, `WaitingForDelivery`, `Verifying`, `Succeeded`, `Denied`, `Failed`, `Expired`, `Cancelled`, `Superseded`, `NeedsIntervention`, `Inconclusive`

Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Pending` | PhasePending means the request was accepted and is waiting for the policy check. |
| `PolicyChecked` | PhasePolicyChecked means the policy allows the plan and the source in Git is resolved. |
| `PRCreated` | PhasePRCreated means the branch and pull request exist. |
| `AwaitingApproval` | PhaseAwaitingApproval means the pull request waits for human review. |
| `AutoMergeQueued` | PhaseAutoMergeQueued means policy allowed automation and auto-merge is enabled on the pull request. |
| `Merged` | PhaseMerged means the pull request is merged. |
| `WaitingForDelivery` | PhaseWaitingForDelivery means the change is merged and the GitOps controller has not applied it yet. |
| `Verifying` | PhaseVerifying means the change is delivered and the verification checks are running. |
| `Succeeded` | PhaseSucceeded means every verification check held for stableFor. Terminal. |
| `Denied` | PhaseDenied means policy refused the plan; no pull request is opened. Terminal. |
| `Failed` | PhaseFailed means a step failed, for example verification did not pass before the timeout. Terminal. |
| `Expired` | PhaseExpired means a step reached its deadline. Terminal. |
| `Cancelled` | PhaseCancelled means the request was cancelled before the change was merged. Terminal. |
| `Superseded` | PhaseSuperseded means a plan input changed, or the ScaledObject is no longer ready, or the module that contributes the action was disabled, so the pull request is closed and a new request is needed. With reason HandedOff (ADR-0028) a replacement took over the pull request instead, which stays open. With reason AnotherRequestMerged (on PlanFresh) another request of the same Incident and target was merged while this one waited, before it took the target lock or opened a pull request. With reason AnotherRequestClosed (on PlanFresh) this one waited behind the target lock of another request for the same target and field (status.queuedBehind) whose pull request was closed without a merge, before it took the lock or opened a pull request. Terminal. |
| `NeedsIntervention` | PhaseNeedsIntervention means the controller cannot continue on its own, for example because the target is not declared in a plain manifest; a human must act. |
| `Inconclusive` | PhaseInconclusive means the change was merged and neither success nor failure could be shown; condition Verified is Unknown and its reason says why, for example NoMergeReceipt when the merge could not be bound to a merge receipt (ADR-0030 section 5). Terminal. |

### RemediationPolicySpec

RemediationPolicySpec is what a policy allows: which namespaces may use it, which targets it covers, which
actions within which bounds, where in Git changes may go, and whether a human must approve. It is owned by
the cluster admin (ADR-0011).


Used by: [RemediationPolicy](#remediationpolicy).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requestNamespaces` | [Name](#name) array | No | requestNamespaces are the namespaces whose RemediationRequests may use this policy. A request from any other namespace is Denied, so being able to create requests somewhere does not grant this policy.<br>Default: `[shadewright-system]`<br>Maximum items: 16<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum items: 1<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`<br>List type: set |
| `targets` | [PolicyTargets](#policytargets) | Yes | targets the policy covers. |
| `actions` | [PolicyAction](#policyaction) array | Yes | actions the policy allows, at most one entry per type. MaxItems follows the size of the action catalog; keeping it small keeps the CEL cost of the bounds rules within the API server's budget.<br>Maximum items: 4<br>Minimum items: 1<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type`<br>Rule: adjustKedaMaxReplicas must be set if and only if type is AdjustKedaMaxReplicas<br>Rule: setContainerMemoryLimit must be set if and only if type is SetContainerMemoryLimit |
| `gitOps` | [PolicyGitOps](#policygitops) | Yes | gitOps limits where changes may be made. |
| `approval` | [ApprovalMode](#approvalmode) | No | approval says whether human review is always required.<br>Default: `Required`<br>One of `Required`, `Optional` |

### RemediationPolicyStatus

RemediationPolicyStatus is reserved for the policy's status. No controller writes it yet: a policy is checked
by the schema and CEL rules when it is applied, and a problem with it shows in the conditions of the
RemediationRequests that use it.


Used by: [RemediationPolicy](#remediationpolicy).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | No | observedGeneration is the generation the status describes. |
| `conditions` | [Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#condition-v1-meta) array | No | conditions are reserved. Nothing writes them yet: an unknown repositoryRef is not reported here but refuses the requests that use the policy (reason RepositoryNotInPolicy).<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type` |

### RemediationRequestSpec

RemediationRequestSpec is one concrete plan. It is immutable: a different plan is a new request, so an
approval can never carry over to a changed plan. It names what to change, not where: the repository, branch
and file are resolved by the controller (ADR-0012), so the author cannot point a change at another file.
Each action type fixes the kinds it may target.


Validation rules:

- spec is immutable; a changed plan is a new RemediationRequest: `self == oldSelf`
- AdjustKedaMaxReplicas can only target a keda.sh ScaledObject: `self.action.type != 'AdjustKedaMaxReplicas' || (self.targetRef.apiVersion.startsWith('keda.sh/') && self.targetRef.kind == 'ScaledObject')`
- SetContainerMemoryLimit can only target an apps/v1 Deployment or StatefulSet: `self.action.type != 'SetContainerMemoryLimit' || (self.targetRef.apiVersion == 'apps/v1' && self.targetRef.kind in ['Deployment', 'StatefulSet'])`
- replaces and chainRoot are set together or not at all: `has(self.replaces) == has(self.chainRoot)`
- a revert (spec.reverts) requires approvalRequired: true: `!has(self.reverts) || (has(self.approvalRequired) && self.approvalRequired)`
- a revert (spec.reverts) never replaces another request: `!has(self.reverts) || !has(self.replaces)`

Used by: [RemediationRequest](#remediationrequest).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `incidentRef` | [IncidentRef](#incidentref) | Yes | incidentRef is the incident this plan answers. |
| `targetRef` | [ObjectRef](#objectref) | Yes | targetRef is the live object the change is about.<br>Rule: targetRef.uid is required (`has(self.uid) && size(self.uid) > 0`)<br>Rule: targetRef.namespace is required (`has(self.namespace) && size(self.namespace) > 0`) |
| `mode` | [RemediationMode](#remediationmode) | No | mode is how the plan is carried out.<br>Default: `GitOps`<br>One of `GitOps` |
| `approvalRequired` | boolean | No | approvalRequired asks for human review. false is a request for automation that policy may refuse; it never lowers policy or repository rules.<br>Default: `true` |
| `policyRef` | [Name](#name) | Yes | policyRef names the RemediationPolicy that must allow this plan.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | Yes | action is the typed change.<br>Rule: adjustKedaMaxReplicas must be set if and only if type is AdjustKedaMaxReplicas<br>Rule: setContainerMemoryLimit must be set if and only if type is SetContainerMemoryLimit |
| `verification` | [Verification](#verification) | No | verification says when the change counts as a success.<br>Default: `{}`<br>Rule: stableFor must be at least 1m<br>Rule: timeout must be at most 24h<br>Rule: timeout must be longer than stableFor |
| `replaces` | [RequestReplacement](#requestreplacement) | No | replaces names the request this one replaces and the reviewer hint of that request it answers (ADR-0028 section 4). Set only by the analyzer on a replacement, together with chainRoot. It is part of the plan, so it is part of the request's name: the same plan answering another hint is another request. The executor checks the link once, at the policy check, and then takes the pull request over (the handoff). |
| `chainRoot` | [UID](#uid) | No | chainRoot is the UID of the first request of the supersede chain: the replaced request's chainRoot, or its own UID when it has none. Set together with replaces. The branch of the pull request derives from it (shadewright/&lt;chainRoot>), so every request of a chain works on the same branch and pull request.<br>Maximum length: 36<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| `reverts` | [RequestRef](#requestref) | No | reverts names the request whose change this one undoes, by name and UID (ADR-0030 section 8). Set only on a revert, which the analyzer's deterministic revert proposer creates, with no model call, for a request that ended Failed with Verified False. A model proposal has no such field. A revert requires approvalRequired: true, never replaces another request, and is never changed after create (the spec is immutable). The executor checks the link before the policy check: the named request exists with this UID, ended Failed with Verified False, is not a revert itself, has the same Incident, target and action type (and container), and this request's previous and desired values are its desired and previous values; this request's name is RevertName of that UID, so a failed request has at most one revert at a time (the proposer also records it in the Incident's status.revertsProposed and never makes a second one). Otherwise the request ends Denied with reason InvalidRevert before any Git write. A revert is never checked for clearing: the verifier writes no report for it, and once rolled out, configured and available for stableFor it ends Inconclusive with reason RevertApplied, never Succeeded. |

### RemediationRequestStatus

RemediationRequestStatus is written only by the remediation controller.


Used by: [RemediationRequest](#remediationrequest).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | No | observedGeneration is the generation the status describes. |
| `phase` | [RemediationPhase](#remediationphase) | No | phase summarizes progress. It is a selectable field (field selector status.phase), so the executor's limits list only the phases they need from the API server.<br>One of `Pending`, `PolicyChecked`, `PRCreated`, `AwaitingApproval`, `AutoMergeQueued`, `Merged`, `WaitingForDelivery`, `Verifying`, `Succeeded`, `Denied`, `Failed`, `Expired`, `Cancelled`, `Superseded`, `NeedsIntervention`, `Inconclusive` |

It is written with the allowed decision and never cleared. The breaker finds a running probe, or one that ended without a success, by this field only; a request without it is not a probe. It is a selectable field (field selector status.breakerProbe). |
| `holdsTarget` | boolean | No | holdsTarget is true while the request holds the executor's lock on its target: it is set in the status write of the allowed decision and cleared only once the request's pull request is known merged or closed, or a look-up by its branch and marker found none of its own open. While it is true no other request on the same target goes through the policy check. Unset on a request not yet decided, and on one written before the field existed; the executor then derives it once from the request's phase and pull request, keeping the lock when in doubt. A refused request gets false with its refusal. It is a selectable field (field selector status.holdsTarget), so the executor's lock reads only holders. |
| `breakerCounts` | boolean | No | breakerCounts says whether the executor's limits still read the request for the circuit breaker. It is set in the status write that ends the request: true for a success (Merged or a later phase), a failure (Failed, NeedsIntervention) or a probe (breakerProbe) that ended in any other way, false for any other end. The executor sets it to false only when a newer request in Succeeded is recorded (breakerClearedBy names it), and back to true when that request is deleted, or when a request whose deletion may still close a pull request (NeedsIntervention, Expired) is being deleted. It is unset while the request has not ended and on one that ended before the field existed; an unset request is read (fail closed), and the executor sets the field once on an ended one from its status. It is a selectable field (field selector status.breakerCounts), so the breaker reads only the outcomes that still count. |
| `breakerClearedBy` | string | No | breakerClearedBy is the name of the request in Succeeded whose success made the executor set breakerCounts to false on this one, written in the same status write. When that request is deleted, its finalizer sets breakerCounts back to true on every request that names it, before the finalizer is removed. It is a selectable field (field selector status.breakerClearedBy).<br>Maximum length: 253 |
| `queuedBehind` | [RequestRef](#requestref) array | No | queuedBehind names the requests that held the lock on the target when the executor last held this one back (Queued, with any reason) while the target was locked, written in that status write (#643). Until the request is decided, it ends Superseded (PlanFresh False, reason AnotherRequestClosed) when a recorded request ended NeedsIntervention because its pull request for the same target and field was closed without a merge. A request that never waited behind that one has no record of it and is decided as usual. Only the executor writes it; once set it is never removed or emptied (a validation rule refuses that). At most four holders are recorded, those for the same field first: a request behind more holders than that may have no record of one, and is then decided as usual when that one's pull request is closed.<br>Maximum items: 4<br>List type: map<br>List key: `uid` |
| `effectiveApprovalRequired` | boolean | No | effectiveApprovalRequired is what policy decided, which may be stricter than spec.approvalRequired. |
| `source` | [ResolvedSource](#resolvedsource) | No | source is where the change is made, resolved by the controller before the policy check. |
| `planDigest` | string | No | planDigest covers the semantic change, the target UID, the resolved source with the repository URL and provider installation from RemediationSettings, and the policy UID and generation. It is fixed when the branch is created; if any input changes later, the request becomes Superseded and its PR is closed.<br>Pattern: `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `planRepository` | [PlanRepository](#planrepository) | No | planRepository is the repository and installation the plan digest covers, set together with planDigest. |

| `policyUID` | [UID](#uid) | No | policyUID is the UID of the policy the decision used. It is part of the plan digest.<br>Maximum length: 36<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
