It is written in the status write that sets Merged and is never changed or removed after (validation rules on the object). A request merged without a full merge commit ID gets none and ends Inconclusive with reason NoMergeReceipt; a merge with a foreign change (MergedWithForeignChange) gets none either. Unset on a request merged before the field existed (condition Verified Unknown, reason MergedBeforeVerification). |
| `mergeCommitAwaitedSince` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | mergeCommitAwaitedSince is when the executor first saw this request's pull request merged without a full merge commit ID, on its own clock. The executor waits for the Git host to report the commit for five minutes from it (GitHub computes it after the merge), keeping the phase, and then records the merge without a receipt (NoMergeReceipt, ending Inconclusive) or, for a pull request it never recorded, as merged with a change it cannot check. Set once and never changed or removed (a validation rule on the object), so a restart does not start the wait again. Unset when the commit was reported at once. |
| `rollout` | [RolloutStatus](#rolloutstatus) | No | rollout is what the check after the merge keeps between reconciles (the RolledOut condition). |
| `deadline` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | deadline is when the current step gives up, on the executor's clock. In WaitingForDelivery it is the end of the delivery window: one hour after mergeReceipt.mergedAt, extended by the time writes were paused. In Verifying it is the timeout, written on entering the phase: status.pullRequest.appliedObservedAt plus the larger of spec.verification.timeout and the rollout deadline plus the effective stableFor plus the executor's --node-grace. Past the merge a deadline never ends a request Expired: the evidence decides between Failed and Inconclusive (ADR-0030 sections 2, 4 and 6). |
| `verification` | [VerificationWindow](#verificationwindow) | No | verification is the executor's own stable window while the request is Verifying (ADR-0030 section 4). Only the executor writes it; once set it is kept, windowStart and the time of lastReset only move forward and resets never decreases (validation rules on the object).<br>Rule: lastReset requires resets of at least 1 |
| `hints` | [Hint](#hint) array | No | hints are the reviewer hints the executor accepted from comments on the pull request, and the hints a replacement carried over from its chain (ADR-0028). Two bounds: at most MaxStoredHints entries in all, and at most MaxHints of them Consumed or Reserved, the hints a supersede chain may consume. Only the executor writes them; a stored hint keeps its pin, moves only forward in its state and is never removed, so a Declined hint stays as the record of what was asked. Planned: carrying them over to a replacement.<br>Maximum items: 10<br>List type: map<br>List key: `source`<br>List key: `commentID`<br>Rule: status.hints: at most 3 hints are Consumed or Reserved (`self.filter(h, h.state in ['Consumed', 'Reserved']).size() <= 3`) |
| `refusedHints` | [RefusedHint](#refusedhint) array | No | refusedHints are the newest comments with the command that the executor refused, at most MaxRefusedHints, oldest first; the oldest one whose reply is recorded is dropped for a new one, and while every one still waits for its reply a new refusal is not recorded. Only the executor writes them.<br>Maximum items: 10<br>List type: map<br>List key: `source`<br>List key: `commentID`<br>Rule: the reply to a refused hint never changes once set |
| `commentCursor` | [CommentCursor](#commentcursor) | No | commentCursor is where the executor's next look at the comments of the pull request starts (ADR-0028 section 3). Only the executor writes it.<br>Rule: etag is kept only on the first page of a new sweep<br>Rule: evictedAt and evictedID are set together |
| `handoff` | [Handoff](#handoff) | No | handoff records the supersede handoff (ADR-0028 section 4): on a replacement, the request it takes over (from); on a predecessor, its replacement (to); a request in the middle of a chain has both. Each side is never removed; Handoff says what may change. Only the executor writes it.<br>Rule: a handoff has from, to or both |
| `conditions` | [Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#condition-v1-meta) array | No | conditions explain the phase. Types: PolicyAllowed, PullRequestOpened, Approved, Delivered, Verified, Configured, Cleared, PlanFresh, WritesPaused, Queued and RolledOut (after the merge: whether the target's pods run the applied template; True with reason RolloutComplete, or RolloutPartitioned when a partitioned StatefulSet keeps pods on the old revision on purpose; False with reason RolloutStuck or DeliveryNotObserved, Unknown while in progress and with reason KindNotChecked, RolloutSuperseded or RolloutNotDetermined when the check ends without a verdict).<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type` |

### RemediationSettingsSpec

RemediationSettingsSpec holds cluster-wide settings, including the kill switch.


Used by: [RemediationSettings](#remediationsettings).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paused` | boolean | No | paused stops every write: pull requests, auto-merge and issues. Analysis continues. Checked right before each write. It revokes no published pull request and reverts no merge; see https://shadewright.io/emergency/.<br>Default: `false` |
| `maxConcurrentRemediations` | integer | No | maxConcurrentRemediations limits the requests that are active at once in the operator namespace: from PolicyChecked up to the merge, and while a deleted one still closes its pull request. A further request the policy allows stays Pending, with the condition Queued, until fewer are active; a refusal at the first check is never held back, but a request already Queued is decided again only once the limits let it through. Read from the API server right before each allowed decision.<br>Default: `1`<br>Maximum: 20<br>Minimum: 1 |
| `maxAnalysesPerDay` | integer | No | maxAnalysesPerDay is deprecated: it moved to spec.analysis.maxAnalysesPerDay. It has no default, and a rule on the field refuses any write that sets or changes it. An object stored by v0.1.0 that holds it can still be updated as long as the value is left as it is (CRD validation ratcheting), and removing it is always allowed. While it is set, the analysis trigger goes by the lower of it and spec.analysis.maxAnalysesPerDay, so an old 0 keeps analysis off. Move the value and remove this field.<br>Maximum: 10000<br>Minimum: 0<br>Rule: spec.maxAnalysesPerDay moved to spec.analysis.maxAnalysesPerDay: set it there and remove this field (`false`) |
| `repositories` | [GitRepository](#gitrepository) array | No | repositories Shadewright may open pull requests in. URLs are unique, so a Flux source matches at most one entry.<br>Maximum items: 16<br>List type: map<br>List key: `name`<br>Rule: repository URLs must be unique (`self.all(r, self.exists_one(s, s.url == r.url))`) |
| `modules` | [Modules](#modules) | No | modules enables platform and integration modules. Left out, only the generic platform is on and no integration is: nothing is enabled because it was detected. |
| `analysis` | [AnalysisSettings](#analysissettings) | No | analysis bounds every model-backed analysis and names the model deployments it may call. Left out, its limits take their defaults and no model is configured. maxAnalysesPerDay is read by the analysis trigger; the analysis loop, which the analyzer starts only with its --triage-model flag, reads and enforces the rest, maxTokensPerDay within one analysis only until the spend counter of #208. The endpoints decide where the analyzer sends its Entra ID token and the redacted context, so write access to this object is security-relevant (threat model).<br>Default: `{}` |

### RemediationSettingsStatus

RemediationSettingsStatus is the analyzer's report of platform and integration detection (ADR-0024). It says
nothing about whether a repository or signer is usable: those are built when a request needs them, and a
problem shows in the conditions of that request.


Used by: [RemediationSettings](#remediationsettings).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | No | observedGeneration is the generation the status describes. |
| `conditions` | [Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#condition-v1-meta) array | No | conditions report problems. The analyzer writes UnknownModules: True when spec.modules names a module that it does not have compiled in, which then contributes nothing; DetectionFailed: True when its last run could not list the nodes or read the discovery API, so the report is from the last run that succeeded, or shows only generic active when none has; and NoWatchedNamespaces: True when it was started with no namespace to watch (the chart's default), so it reads no events or pods and records no Incident; and SymptomSourcesNotWatched: True when an active module declares a symptom source for a kind the collector does not watch (not served, not granted, or the check or the watch failed), Unknown while such a kind has not been checked yet, set only while it watches namespaces. A kind whose optional grant the chart leaves out on purpose (the Kyverno cluster-wide kinds) is not reported.<br>List type: map<br>List key: `type` |
| `platform` | [PlatformStatus](#platformstatus) | No | platform is the platform the analyzer detected and the one it uses. The analyzer writes it at start, when spec changes, every 10 minutes, and when the watch state of a symptom source kind changes (ADR-0024), with the only write it has outside the operator namespace. Status is a report, never an input: no component reads any field of it to decide anything.<br>Rule: detected is left out, not generic, when no platform claims the cluster<br>Rule: active is generic or the detected platform |
| `integrations` | [IntegrationStatus](#integrationstatus) array | No | integrations lists every integration module that is enabled or detected, with whether it is active. A detected add-on whose module is not enabled is listed too, so the cluster admin sees what could be enabled. Written like platform. At most 64: 32 enabled (the spec cap) and 32 more detected, since a detected add-on needs a compiled-in module and internal/modules refuses more than 32.<br>Maximum items: 64<br>List type: map<br>List key: `name`<br>Rule: version is set if and only if the integration is detected<br>Rule: an integration that is not detected is not active |

### ResetReason

ResetReason says why a verification window was reset (ADR-0030 section 4). The verifier sets Restarted,
PodNotReady, PartialRollout, EvidenceMissing, ScaledToZero and ObservationGap in its report, the only reasons
the enum of WindowReset.reason accepts. NotAvailable, StaleReport and ReportMismatch are the executor's
reasons for its own window; with PartialRollout they are the reasons of status.verification.lastReset of a
RemediationRequest (VerificationReset), never of a report.

- Underlying type: string

Used by: [VerificationReset](#verificationreset), [WindowReset](#windowreset).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Restarted` | ResetRestarted: a container of a pod of the rollout (a native sidecar included) restarted above its baseline, or terminated after the window started. Trouble class; recorded in troubleResets only for a restart count above its baseline after the window first opened. |
| `PodNotReady` | ResetPodNotReady: a pod of the rollout is not Ready and did not restart. No evidence. |
| `PartialRollout` | ResetPartialRollout: fewer pods on the applied revision than the desired replicas, or a pod of the target on another revision; for the executor, a report that does not cover every desired replica. No evidence. |
| `EvidenceMissing` | ResetEvidenceMissing: a pod without a status for every container, more pods than the bound, or a target that is not the one the report names. No evidence. |
| `ScaledToZero` | ResetScaledToZero: the target's spec.replicas is 0. No evidence. |
| `ObservationGap` | ResetObservationGap: no sample for more than two poll intervals, and a pod not in the baselines after it. No evidence. |
| `NotAvailable` | ResetNotAvailable: the target reports other available replicas than desired, fewer or more (executor). No evidence. |
| `StaleReport` | ResetStaleReport: the report is missing or its sample counter stopped rising (executor). No evidence. |
| `ReportMismatch` | ResetReportMismatch: the report's spec names another request, merge commit, target or template revision (executor). No evidence. |

### ResolvedSource

ResolvedSource is where the controller found the target's declaration in Git (ADR-0012). It is derived from
the Flux objects that deliver the target and from RemediationSettings, never taken from the request.


Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repositoryRef` | [Name](#name) | Yes | repositoryRef is the RemediationSettings entry whose URL matches the Flux source.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `targetBranch` | [GitBranch](#gitbranch) | Yes | targetBranch is the branch the pull request targets: the branch Flux tracks, which must equal the repository's targetBranch in RemediationSettings.<br>Maximum length: 255<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*$`<br>Rule: must be a plain branch name, not HEAD, refs/..., shadewright/... or one containing '..' or '.lock' |
| `path` | [GitFilePath](#gitfilepath) | Yes | path is the file that declares the target.<br>Maximum length: 512<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*\.ya?ml$` |

Before every commit the pull request step renders it with and without the change and refuses anything but the planned difference (design 8.2, steps 4 and 5). The policy check always sets it, and the plan digest covers it; a request without it is never committed.<br>Maximum length: 512<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: <code>^(\.&#124;&#91;A-Za-z0-9_]&#91;A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(/&#91;A-Za-z0-9_]&#91;A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)*)$</code> |
| `baseCommit` | string | Yes | baseCommit is the full SHA of the target branch the change was made against. It is fixed when the branch is created; later merges to the target branch do not change it.<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |

### RevertState

### ReviewCheck

ReviewCheck is the check run shadewright/review on one head of the pull request (ADR-0028 section 5),
pinned to that head: a state recorded for one head never counts for another. Every head the executor pushes
or adopts starts without one, and the executor creates the check in progress on it. On one head the state
moves only from InProgress to Passed, Failed or Refused.


Validation rules:

- on one head the check run moves only from InProgress to Passed, Failed or Refused: `self.head != oldSelf.head || self.state == oldSelf.state || (oldSelf.state == 'InProgress' && self.state in ['Passed', 'Failed', 'Refused'])`

Used by: [PullRequestStatus](#pullrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `head` | string | Yes | head is the commit the check run is on, always the pull request's recorded head (headSHA).<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `state` | [ReviewCheckState](#reviewcheckstate) | Yes | state is how far the check run on head has come.<br>One of `InProgress`, `Passed`, `Failed`, `Refused` |

### ReviewCheckState

ReviewCheckState is how far the check run shadewright/review of a head has come (ADR-0028 section 5).
InProgress: created, in progress, waiting for an approval of the head by someone who wrote no hint in the
chain. Passed: completed with conclusion success after such an approval. Failed: completed with conclusion
failure because the merge gate could not read every review of the pull request, so it fails closed on this
head and a person decides the merge. Refused: the Git host refused to create or complete it for good, so the
required check does not pass on this head and the pull request cannot merge until a person acts.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `InProgress`, `Passed`, `Failed`, `Refused`

Used by: [ReviewCheck](#reviewcheck).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `InProgress` |  |
| `Passed` |  |
| `Failed` |  |
| `Refused` |  |

### RolloutStatus

RolloutStatus is what the check after the merge records about the target's rollout. Only the executor writes
it; once status.rollout exists it is never removed, each field is set once and never changed (pausedSince is
only set or cleared, never moved, and pausedSeconds never decreases), and ended never goes back to false.
These rules sit on the RemediationRequest, so that dropping rollout, or the whole status, and writing it again
cannot reopen the check or move its window.

The rollout judged is the one the applied commit produced: the executor reads the target right after the
GitOps controller reports the commit applied and records, in the same status write as
status.pullRequest.appliedObservedAt, the commit applied (appliedRevision), the target's generation
(targetGeneration) and a hash of its pod template (templateHash). A later commit of the target branch that holds
the merge commit counts as ours: the template it produced is judged. A change made outside Git (kubectl edit,
another controller) is not told apart from a Git one when it lands before that read, so it is not covered.


Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `waitStartedAt` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | waitStartedAt is when the executor started waiting for the delivery of a merged request that has no lastPhaseTransitionTime; the delivery window is then measured from it instead of from the merge. |
| `pausedSince` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | pausedSince is when the executor first saw writes paused (RemediationSettings spec.paused) while it waited for the delivery; cleared when it sees them resumed, the paused time then added to pausedSeconds. It is never moved while set. |
| `pausedSeconds` | integer | No | pausedSeconds is how long, in seconds, writes were paused while the executor waited for the delivery; the delivery window is extended by it (and by the pause still running), so a pause never uses up the window. It never decreases.<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `appliedRevision` | string | No | appliedRevision is the commit the GitOps controller reported applied when the executor first saw the merge commit delivered: the merge commit, or a later commit of the target branch that holds it.<br>Maximum length: 40<br>Minimum length: 40<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `targetGeneration` | integer | No | targetGeneration is the target's metadata.generation read right after appliedRevision was seen applied: the generation the applied commit produced.<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `templateHash` | string | No | templateHash is the SHA-256 of the target's pod template at targetGeneration. When the target's controller first reports a generation past targetGeneration, the revision it names is recorded only if the template is still this one; otherwise the check ends with RolledOut Unknown, reason RolloutSuperseded.<br>Maximum length: 64<br>Minimum length: 64<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `templateRevision` | string | No | templateRevision is the template revision the check judges: a StatefulSet's status.updateRevision or a Deployment's deployment.kubernetes.io/revision annotation, read once the controller observed targetGeneration and the target's current generation (a revision annotation can name a later generation before the status does), and, past targetGeneration, only while the template still matches templateHash. A newer revision ends the check with RolledOut Unknown, reason RolloutSuperseded.<br>Maximum length: 253 |
| `ended` | boolean | No | ended is true once the check gave its final verdict in RolledOut; nothing is read for it after that. |

### SetContainerMemoryLimit

SetContainerMemoryLimit changes resources.limits.memory of one container. previous must match the file in
Git when the patch is applied, or the plan is stale. Both values are whole bytes between 1Mi and 1Ti. The
rules compare a value only once its approximate float is between -2e12 and 2e12: the quantity library would
compute a huge decimal exponent digit by digit, for either sign (#593).


Validation rules:

- desired must differ from previous: `!(quantity(string(self.previous)).asApproximateFloat() >= -2e12 && quantity(string(self.previous)).asApproximateFloat() <= 2e12 && quantity(string(self.desired)).asApproximateFloat() >= -2e12 && quantity(string(self.desired)).asApproximateFloat() <= 2e12) || quantity(string(self.desired)).compareTo(quantity(string(self.previous))) != 0`
- previous and desired must be whole bytes: `!(quantity(string(self.previous)).asApproximateFloat() >= -2e12 && quantity(string(self.previous)).asApproximateFloat() <= 2e12 && quantity(string(self.desired)).asApproximateFloat() >= -2e12 && quantity(string(self.desired)).asApproximateFloat() <= 2e12) || (quantity(string(self.previous)).isInteger() && quantity(string(self.desired)).isInteger())`
- previous must be between 1Mi and 1Ti: `quantity(string(self.previous)).asApproximateFloat() >= -2e12 && quantity(string(self.previous)).asApproximateFloat() <= 2e12 && quantity(string(self.previous)).compareTo(quantity('1Mi')) >= 0 && quantity(string(self.previous)).compareTo(quantity('1Ti')) <= 0`
- desired must be between 1Mi and 1Ti: `quantity(string(self.desired)).asApproximateFloat() >= -2e12 && quantity(string(self.desired)).asApproximateFloat() <= 2e12 && quantity(string(self.desired)).compareTo(quantity('1Mi')) >= 0 && quantity(string(self.desired)).compareTo(quantity('1Ti')) <= 0`

Used by: [Action](#action).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | string | Yes | container is the container name in the pod template.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Minimum length: 1<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `previous` | [Quantity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#quantity-resource-core) | Yes | previous is the limit the plan was made against. |
| `desired` | [Quantity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#quantity-resource-core) | Yes | desired is the new limit. |

UID is a Kubernetes object UID in its canonical lower-case form. MaxLength states the bound the pattern
already holds, so the API server can bound the cost of CEL rules that read the field.

### Verification

Verification says when a delivered change counts as a success. The controller always adds the checks the
action type needs (DeliveryRevisionApplied, plus KedaReady or NoNewOOMKills), so a request can only make
verification stricter.


Validation rules:

- stableFor must be at least 1m: `!has(self.stableFor) || duration(self.stableFor) >= duration('1m')`
- timeout must be at most 24h: `!has(self.timeout) || duration(self.timeout) <= duration('24h')`
- timeout must be longer than stableFor: `!has(self.timeout) || !has(self.stableFor) || duration(self.timeout) > duration(self.stableFor)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestSpec](#remediationrequestspec).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout` | [Duration](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1#Duration) | No | timeout is how long to wait for delivery and stability before giving up.<br>Default: `10m` |
| `stableFor` | [Duration](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1#Duration) | No | stableFor is how long all checks must hold.<br>Default: `3m` |
| `checks` | [VerificationCheck](#verificationcheck) array | No | checks to run in addition to the ones the action type always needs.<br>One of `DeliveryRevisionApplied`, `WorkloadHealthy`, `KedaReady`, `QueueBacklogDecreasing`, `NoNewOOMKills`<br>Maximum items: 8<br>List type: set |

### VerificationCheck

VerificationCheck is a named, deterministic check run after delivery. DeliveryRevisionApplied: the GitOps
controller has applied the revision that contains the merged change. WorkloadHealthy: the target workload
is available and its rollout is complete. KedaReady: the KEDA ScaledObject reports Ready=True, is not
paused (Paused=True, which a scale-in or scale-out pause also sets), is not on fallback (Fallback=True) and
its HPA can read its metrics (HPAActive is not False). QueueBacklogDecreasing: the backlog that drives the
ScaledObject is going down. NoNewOOMKills: no container of the target is OOMKilled after the change.

- Underlying type: string
- One of `DeliveryRevisionApplied`, `WorkloadHealthy`, `KedaReady`, `QueueBacklogDecreasing`, `NoNewOOMKills`

Used by: [Verification](#verification).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `DeliveryRevisionApplied` |  |
| `WorkloadHealthy` |  |
| `KedaReady` |  |
| `QueueBacklogDecreasing` |  |
| `NoNewOOMKills` |  |

### VerificationReportSpec

VerificationReportSpec binds a report to one request, its merge, its target and the template revision it
judges. It is set when the verifier creates the report and never changes. It holds no time of the executor's
clock.


Validation rules:

- spec is immutable: `self == oldSelf`

Used by: [VerificationReport](#verificationreport).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requestUID` | [UID](#uid) | Yes | requestUID is the UID of the RemediationRequest the report is about.<br>Maximum length: 36<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| `mergeCommitSHA` | string | Yes | mergeCommitSHA is the merge commit of the request's merge receipt.<br>Maximum length: 40<br>Minimum length: 40<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` |
| `targetUID` | [UID](#uid) | Yes | targetUID is the UID of the target workload.<br>Maximum length: 36<br>Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| `templateRevision` | string | Yes | templateRevision is the template revision of the rollout, from the request's status.rollout: a Deployment's revision annotation or a StatefulSet's update revision.<br>Maximum length: 253<br>Minimum length: 1 |
| `container` | string | No | container is the name of the action's container, for an action that names one (SetContainerMemoryLimit). An OOM kill of this container ends the request Failed.<br>Maximum length: 63<br>Pattern: `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` |

### VerificationReportStatus

VerificationReportStatus is the verifier's pod-level window: its samples, its resets, its restart baselines
and an OOM kill once seen. Typed fields only: nothing is copied from the cluster as text.


Used by: [VerificationReport](#verificationreport).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sample` | integer | No | sample counts the samples written: the verifier raises it by one with every sample. It never decreases. The executor judges the age of the report by this counter on its own clock, never by sampledAt.<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `sampledAt` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | sampledAt is when the last sample was taken, on the verifier's clock. |
| `windowStart` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | windowStart is the time of the first good sample of the current window, on the verifier's clock. It only moves forward. The window is open while windowStart is later than lastReset.time; its span is sampledAt - windowStart. |
| `desiredReplicas` | integer | No | desiredReplicas is the target's spec.replicas at the last sample.<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `podsCovered` | integer | No | podsCovered is the number of pods of the rollout at the last sample: pods whose ownership by the target was proven and that run the report's template revision.<br>Maximum: 200<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `resets` | integer | No | resets counts the resets of the window. It never decreases.<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `lastReset` | [WindowReset](#windowreset) | No | lastReset is the last reset of the window. Once set it is kept, and its time never moves back. |
| `troubleResets` | integer | No | troubleResets counts the Restarted resets recorded as trouble over the life of the report: those with a restart count above its baseline after the window first opened (the first good sample). A Restarted reset before that, or one shown only by a termination time (a node's clock), is not counted. It never decreases: a later no-evidence reset does not hide that a restart was observed.<br>Minimum: 0 |
| `lastTroubleReset` | [WindowReset](#windowreset) | No | lastTroubleReset is the last Restarted reset recorded as trouble. Once set it is kept, and its time never moves back. A report that records trouble ends its request Failed at the timeout, whatever its last reset.<br>Rule: lastTroubleReset.reason must be Restarted (`self.reason == 'Restarted'`) |
| `oomKill` | [OOMKill](#oomkill) | No | oomKill is the first OOM kill of the action's container on a pod of the rollout. Once set it never changes. |
| `baselines` | [PodBaseline](#podbaseline) array | No | baselines are the restart baselines of the pods, one per pod UID, at most 200. A baseline whose pod is gone from the pod list is pruned in the same write.<br>Maximum items: 200<br>List type: map<br>List key: `podUID` |

### VerificationReset

VerificationReset is a reset of the executor's own verification window (ADR-0030 section 4): a check of a
Verifying request that was not good.


Used by: [VerificationWindow](#verificationwindow).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | [ResetReason](#resetreason) | Yes | reason says why the window was reset: NotAvailable (the target reports other available replicas than desired, fewer or more, a revert's target desires no replica, or a ScaledObject is not ready by the KedaReady rule), StaleReport (the verifier's report is missing, was never sampled, or its sample counter stopped rising), ReportMismatch (the report names another request, merge commit, target, template revision or container) or PartialRollout (the report does not cover every desired replica, or a revert is checked before RolledOut is True). Every one is a reset of the no-evidence class.<br>One of `NotAvailable`, `StaleReport`, `ReportMismatch`, `PartialRollout` |
| `time` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | Yes | time is when the reset was recorded, on the executor's clock. It is never earlier than windowStart at that moment or the previous reset, so the window is open only while windowStart is later than it. |

### VerificationWindow

VerificationWindow is the executor's own stable window of a Verifying request (ADR-0030 section 4), kept next
to the verifier's window in the VerificationReport. Every time in it is on the executor's clock, and it is
never compared with a time of the report. No window counts time from before the executor process began reconciling, so after a restart or a leader change every open window needs a full stableFor again. A lastReset is
counted: resets is at least 1 when it is set.


Validation rules:

- lastReset requires resets of at least 1: `!has(self.lastReset) || (has(self.resets) && self.resets >= 1)`

Used by: [RemediationRequestStatus](#remediationrequeststatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `windowStart` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | No | windowStart is when the current window opened: the first good check after the last reset. It only moves forward. |
| `lastReset` | [VerificationReset](#verificationreset) | No | lastReset is the last reset of the window. Kept once set; its time never moves back. |
| `resets` | integer | No | resets counts the resets of the window: a bad check that closes an open window or names another reason than lastReset. The same reason again on a closed window is not counted and writes nothing. It never decreases, and it is at least 1 while lastReset is set.<br>Minimum: 0 |

### WindowReset

WindowReset is a reset of a verification window. Its class (Restarted is trouble, every other reason no
evidence) follows from reason and is not stored.


Used by: [VerificationReportStatus](#verificationreportstatus).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | [ResetReason](#resetreason) | Yes | reason says why the window was reset: one of the reasons the verifier sets.<br>One of `Restarted`, `PodNotReady`, `PartialRollout`, `EvidenceMissing`, `ScaledToZero`, `ObservationGap` |
| `time` | [Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#time-v1-meta) | Yes | time is when the reset was recorded, on the clock of the writer of the window. It is never earlier than the window's start at that moment or the previous reset, so a window is open only while windowStart is later than it. |
